Sina Finance (keyless) — A-share breadth: pct_above_50, pct_above_200, NH/NL, A/D line (Hu-Shen A-share board)
China Stock Connect data (collectors/china_connect.py) — daily southbound/northbound net flows; northbound frozen since 2024-08-16
HKMA public JSON API (keyless) — aggregate balance, O/N HIBOR, TWI, base rate, peg bands

BoC VALET API (keyless) + StatsCan + FRED comparables — Canada: policy rate, CORRA, CPI YoY, GoC 2y/5y/10y yields, GoC RRB, USD/CAD BoC, unemployment (LFS), monthly real GDP, house prices, CAD REER, US 2y/10y
FRED OECD CSV (keyless) + ECB — Intl macro: per-country yield_10y, short_3m, cpi_yoy, unemployment, gdp, m2; ECB depo rate, periphery spreads (DE/IT/ES/FR 10y)
Shenwan L1 industry indices (collectors/china_sectors.py) — 31 sector OHLCV tapes back to 1999/2014/2021 (group china_sectors)
HK constituent breadth cache (data/hk_breadth/_closes_cache.parquet) — ~160 names, ~3y rolling window for synthetic sector baskets
gaps: L1 — No base-effect forecasting for any intl market. The 63d YoY diff sign (china_axes.py:32-38, intl_regime.py:45-49) measures first-derivative direction of the most recently released print — it captures the current RoC but not the deterministic forward path. A base period fully known 12 months ahead is never computed; the system cannot project whether the YoY will mechanically accelerate or decelerate into future quarters even for stable sequential momentum.

L1 — Monthly macro inputs are latest-revision only with aggressive forward-fill (40d for China PMI/CPI, 130d for GDP, 260d for LPR in china_inputs.py:94-100). Backtests and live readings differ in data vintage. No ALFRED/Philly real-time vintages, no StatsCan initial-release vs revised tracking, no point-in-time replay for any country. The split-half calibration (calibrate_china.py, split_date=2016-01-01) uses the same revised data in both halves — this systematically overstates historical stability.

L1 — No mixed-frequency dynamic factor model (Kalman/DFM) or MIDAS for any intl market. The axis score is a static weighted average of discretized (thresholded) individual components. There is no daily growth/inflation state with a variance estimate; the 'regime_confidence' (mean of two axis confidences) is an ad-hoc agreement score, not a posterior probability.

L2 — Regime output is a discrete argmax quad (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4) via apply_hysteresis (regime.py:41-76), not a probability distribution P(Quad_k). There is no Markov-switching or HMM. No transition matrix P(Quad_j next | Quad_i now) is estimated or displayed for any intl market. No time-in-regime hazard function. The hysteresis state machine has two scalar tunables (7 days, shock_z=0.85) identical across all four engines — no per-country calibration of these parameters.

L2 — Liquidity and policy are overlays attached post-hoc (china_regime.py:69, hk_regime.py:105, canada_regime.py:71, intl_regime.py:155) not axes in the regime quadrant. They are string-valued categorical labels (expanding/neutral/contracting/unknown) not scored into the growth x inflation decision. This means a PBoC credit tightening cycle does not shift the quad and a BoC emergency cut does not shift the quad — they are decorative.

L3 — No regime-conditional expected-value engine exists for any intl market. The quad classification output feeds the sector_preferences map (config sector_preferences per quad name) which is a static lookup — not empirically estimated forward return distributions mu_{a,k} per quad per asset. No E[r_a] = sum_k P(Quad_k) * mu_{a,k} * intensity_k is computed. The china_sector_pathway.py Wilson-CI conditional odds is the closest approximation (for 4 GS-style sectors only, honest display-only framing) but it uses a binary setup composite as the conditioning variable, not the quad regime.

L3 — No regime-intensity weighting. The quad argmax treats Q1 with growth_score=+0.05 and Q1 with growth_score=+0.85 identically. The score magnitude |growth_score|, |inflation_score| is available but is not used to weight allocation sizing or to scale expected-value estimates. Intensity is discarded at the argmax step.

L4 — No forward volatility model for any intl market. Realized vol is used in country_cycles.py for ZigZag threshold scaling (_zz_pct_for) but this is a noise-filter not a forward vol forecast. No Yang-Zhang OHLC realized vol, no HAR-RV, no GARCH forward surface. No IV surface exists for China/HK/Canada/Intl (no options data is collected). No forward price range is computed as a conditional quantile. The heuristic cycle projection (median half-cycle next-turn) in sector_cycles/_record_core is explicitly labeled a rhythm estimate 'NOT backtested.'

L5 — No mechanical-flow front-running for any intl market. China has northbound Stock Connect data but it is frozen since 2024-08-16 (china_inputs.py:107-113). Southbound is live (HK) but used only as a directional binary in the liquidity overlay — no flow rate-of-change, no extreme reading detection, no CTA positioning proxy, no EM fund flow data. No COT for any intl commodity (Canada: WTI/copper). No options positioning for any intl market.

L6 — The split-half calibration (calibrate_china.py, split_date=2016, calibrate_hk.py, canada calibration via canada.engine.calibration block) shows component weights were adjusted based on return-relationship stability, which is the right intent. But the validation uses revised data (gap 1), simple IC/return sign checks, and no purged K-fold, embargo, deflated Sharpe, or PBO on any intl engine. The china_sector_pathway Phase-0 FWER test is the only statistically honest forward-return analysis in the entire intl stack; there is no equivalent for HK sector, Canada sector, or intl country engines.

L6 — The intl recession composite (intl_regime.py:112-130) is explicitly labeled DISPLAY-ONLY with history-anchored thresholds (elevated_band=45, high_band=65 in config:4723). No Estrella-Mishkin logit, no factor-model recession probability, no forward-return validation by recession_score band for any of the 24 countries. The bands were not derived from any historical back-test of realized recessions.

L7 — No portfolio construction layer for any intl market beyond the china_masterminds.py GTAA (A-share only). No HK, Canada, or intl GTAA book exists. Country allocation across the 24 intl markets is purely display-only (RS rank vs SPY). No HRP, no Black-Litterman, no CVaR constraint, no vol-target for any intl cross-country allocation. The china_masterminds W_REGIME=0.40 regime weight is a fixed prior, not derived from any L3 conditional-EV calibration.

Architecture — All four intl regime engines use identical hysteresis (7 days, shock_z=0.85) and identical scoring params (slope_window=20, baseline_window=60, z_threshold=0.45) regardless of country. A-share markets (faster-moving, policy-shock prone) and European DM economies (slow-moving, monthly data only) have the same confirmation window. No per-country adaptive tuning.

Architecture — country_cycles.py (24 ETFs + 7 aggregates) is completely decoupled from intl_regime.py. A country's cycle phase (early/mid/late via _record_core ZigZag) has no connection to its quad regime. A country can be in Q4 Growth-scare while showing 'early' cycle — the two readings never interact in the output JSON.

Architecture — HK growth axis uses China NBS PMI (pmi_mfg level vs 50) as its primary economic input (hk_axes.py:55), not HK's own Markit PMI. This is theoretically defensible (HSI earnings are China-driven) but means HK regime reads identically to China on the PMI leg — the HK-specific deterioration (e.g. outflows from peg pressure without China PMI move) is only partially captured by hshare_hsi and global_score.

upgrades.title: Deterministic YoY base-effect projection for China CPI/PPI/PMI
upgrades.spec: Add engine/china_base_effect.py. For CPI YoY and PPI YoY: given the latest monthly print and a simple AR(1) MoM momentum assumption (tunable), project 1-3 quarter forward YoY path as: fwd_yoy[t+k] = sequential_fwd[t+k] / base_period[t+k-12]. Compute 2nd derivative of the projected YoY path (sign = accelerating vs decelerating). Expose as growth_2nd_deriv and inflation_2nd_deriv fields on the china_regime output. For PMI use trailing 3-month average as the sequential momentum assumption. No revision risk since the base is a historical print already in the store. Wire into china_axes.py as two new half-weight components (weight 0.5 each) alongside the existing direction scores. Same pattern for HK (reuses China macro) and Canada (BoC CPI).
deps: china_inputs.py already stores cpi_yoy/ppi_yoy monthly with 40d ffill

upgrades.title: Regime probability distribution via Markov-switching (China primary, intl secondary)
upgrades.spec: Add engine/china_regime_msm.py using statsmodels.tsa.regime_switching.markov_switching.MarkovRegression (or hmmlearn GaussianHMM) fit on the daily [growth_score, inflation_score] bivariate series from china_axes. 4-state model (Q1-Q4). Emit: P(Quad_k) for each day (4 floats summing to 1), transition_matrix (4x4), time_in_regime_d (days since last confirmed transition), hazard (probability of transition within 5 days using empirical dwell-time distribution). Store output as data/regime/china_regime_probs.parquet. Replace the single 'quad' field with a P(quad) distribution on the china.html regime card, keeping the argmax as 'current_regime' for backward compat. Port same approach to HK (hk_regime_msm.py) after China validates. Intl engine: apply to the 5 largest economies (JP, DE, UK, KR, TW) only due to thin macro data.

upgrades.title: Score liquidity/policy as a third axis in the China/HK/Canada quad
upgrades.spec: In china_axes.py add score_axis(f, 'liquidity') using existing M2 YoY ROC and LPR direction already in the feature frame. Score as slope_z, same machinery. Add 'liquidity_score' as a third dimension of the regime state (not a 4th argmax quadrant — surface as a signed float -1..+1 modulating the quad confidence, e.g. Q1 Goldilocks with liquidity_score=-0.8 = 'Q1 but credit tightening'). Write as (quad, liquidity_score) tuple in the output JSON. For HK: add HIBOR ON overnight rate 20d direction as an additional liquidity component (already in hk_inputs.py:138). For Canada: add BoC meeting date as a step-change trigger (already in canada_macro MACRO_COLS). Display the liquidity_score as a slider on the regime card.
deps: china_inputs.py: m2_yoy, rate_3m, lpr_1y already present

upgrades.title: Regime-conditional forward return distributions for China sector allocation
upgrades.spec: Add engine/china_regime_ev.py. For each Shenwan L1 sector and each quad (Q1-Q4): estimate mu_{sector, quad} = mean 21d and 63d forward return conditional on being in that quad, using the existing Shenwan deep history (data/china_sectors/ back to 1999). Use point-in-time quad labels from the causal expanding standardization already in china_sector_pathway._expanding_z. Compute CVaR at 95% for each (sector, quad) cell. Output: data/regime/china_regime_ev.json keyed {sector: {Q1: {mu_21d, cvar_21d, n_obs}, ...}}. Wire into china_sector_desk.py: annotate each sector row with E[r] under current P(quad) distribution from L2 upgrade. Rank sectors by E[r]/CVaR as a 'Regime-fit' column. For china_masterminds.py: replace the static sector_preferences lookup with the dynamic E[r]/CVaR ranking as the regime conviction signal (W_REGIME=0.40 block). Validate with purged K-fold (60d embargo, 5 folds) and report rank-IC per fold.

upgrades.title: Regime-conditional return distributions for HK sectors and Canada sectors
upgrades.spec: Port china_regime_ev.py to HK (engine/hk_regime_ev.py) and Canada (engine/canada_regime_ev.py). For HK: use the deep synthetic sector baskets already in hk_inputs.constituent_closes (15-25y history) as return series; condition on hk_regime.classify quad + global_score tercile (Risk-on/off/Neutral) as a 2D conditioning cell — the HK-specific insight is that global_score is the primary driver, so E[r | quad, global_score] is more informative than E[r | quad] alone. For Canada: use TSX sector ETFs (XEG, XMA, XIT etc.); condition on quad + commodity regime (oil/gold slope_z sign) given Canada's commodity-cyclical structure. Report n_obs and Wilson-CI per cell; suppress display when n<15.
deps: hk_inputs.constituent_closes (~3y only — likely thin per-cell n; use non-parametric bootstrap CI)
canada_inputs.py sector ETF closes from canada_closes()

upgrades.title: Point-in-time regime labels for China split-half and walk-forward validation
upgrades.spec: In scripts/calibrate_china.py, replace the current split-half with a walk-forward that generates regime labels using only data available as of the scoring date. Concretely: for each date t in the validation window, refit axis scores and quad classification using only data through t (the store already has the raw monthly prints date-indexed — simply truncate). Compute the 63d forward return as of t. Run purged K-fold (embargo=63d, 5 folds) on the (regime_label_t, forward_return_{t+63d}) pairs. Report: rank-IC per fold, deflated Sharpe on the regime-conditional sector rotation signal, PBO score (fraction of permuted IS Sharpes exceeding OOS). Write output to data/regime/china_validation_report.json and surface as a collapsible 'Validation' panel on china.html. Same structure for HK (calibrate_hk.py) and Canada.
deps: china_inputs.py historical parquet store (no ALFRED needed — prints are date-stamped by NBS release date already)

upgrades.title: Forward volatility surface for China/HK: HAR-RV daily forecast
upgrades.spec: Add engine/china_vol_forecast.py. Compute Yang-Zhang OHLC realized vol (daily) from china_sector_index.sw_close OHLCV (Shenwan data has full OHLCV). Fit HAR-RV model (RV_t = alpha + beta_d*RV_{t-1} + beta_w*RV_{5d_avg} + beta_m*RV_{22d_avg} + eps) per sector using statsmodels OLS with expanding window. Forecast 5d and 22d forward RV with confidence interval. Expose as vol_hat_5d, vol_hat_22d, vol_ci_lo, vol_ci_hi on each Shenwan sector record in china_sector_desk.py. For China GTAA (china_masterminds.py): use vol_hat_22d as the denominator in inverse-vol sizing instead of trailing 22d realized vol — reduces sizing into vol spikes. For HK: use ^HSIL VHSI (already collected in hk_inputs.py:129) as the IV input to a simple GARCH(1,1) on HSI realized vol.
deps: Shenwan L1 OHLCV data (data/china_sectors/*.parquet has full OHLCV)
statsmodels (already in requirements for MSM upgrade)

upgrades.title: Adaptive hysteresis and scoring windows per-country for intl engine
upgrades.spec: In intl_regime.py:score_axis and classify, replace the single config.intl.engine.scoring block with a per-country scoring dict. For fast EM markets (Turkey TUR, Brazil EWZ, Korea EWY): reduce slope_window to 10d and hysteresis_days to 3 (A-share-like dynamics). For slow DM monthly-data-only economies (Germany EWG, France EWQ, Switzerland EWL): increase baseline_window to 120d and hysteresis_days to 14 to avoid noise-flipping on monthly print releases. Add country-level overrides to config.yml under intl.countries.<CC>.engine (optional block, absent = use default). Measure: count regime flip frequency per country on historical series; targets are 4-8 flips/year for DM, 8-15 for EM.

upgrades.title: Link country_cycles phase to intl_regime quad for composite country view
upgrades.spec: In country_cycles._build_one(), after sc._record_core runs, call intl_regime.classify() on the country's feature frame (from intl_inputs.country_frame(cc)) and attach quad, quad_confidence, liquidity, and recession_score to the rec dict. In the compute() output JSON: each country record gains a 'regime' sub-object. In site/intl_cycles.html: the country chip gains a regime badge (Q1 Goldilocks = green, Q4 = red etc.) and a mini-confidence bar. This creates the combined 'cycle phase + regime quad' read that Hedgeye sells as the core dashboard view — currently the two are completely decoupled. Performance: classify() is already computed per country in intl_run.py; cache and reuse, don't recompute.

upgrades.title: Mechanical-flow front-running: Stock Connect extreme reading + HKMA peg-defense trigger
upgrades.spec: In hk_inputs.py: compute southbound_z = southbound_cum.diff(20) z-scored vs its 252d history. Add southbound_extreme (|z|>2) and southbound_direction (sign). In hk_regime.classify(): attach southbound_z and southbound_extreme to the output. For the HK global risk overlay (hk_global.py): add a 4th peg-defense leg: when HKMA Aggregate Balance (agg_balance in hk_inputs.py:135) drops >20% over 5d, flag peg_defense_active=True. In the dashboard hero: show a 'Peg Defense Active' alert when True (precedent: 2022 HKMA intervention). For China: add northbound_cum 20d change as a display-only context signal (frozen since 2024-08-16 but prior period is informative for cycle analysis). For Canada: add weekly Commitments of Traders large-spec WTI net position (CFTC via FRED keyless, series DCOILWTICO_NET) as a commodity positioning extreme signal in canada_overlay.py.
deps: hk_inputs.py agg_balance already collected from HKMA API
southbound_cum already in both china_inputs and hk_inputs

upgrades.title: Portfolio construction for intl country allocation: HRP + regime-driven gross/net dial
upgrades.spec: Add engine/intl_gtaa.py. Universe: the 24 single-country ETFs from country_cycles.COUNTRIES. Inputs: (a) 63d RS vs SPY rank from country_cycles._rank_rs, (b) regime quad from intl_regime.classify per country, (c) recession_score per country. Construction: HRP base weights (scipy.cluster.hierarchy on the 252d correlation matrix of USD-denominated ETF returns). Regime tilt: multiply HRP weight by a regime factor = 1 + 0.3 * (1 - recession_score/100) for Q1/Q2 countries, 0.7 for Q3/Q4. Gross/net dial: if median recession_score across universe > 60, scale all weights down by 0.5 and add EEM short weight (display-only hedge, not executable). Vol-target: scale book to 10% annualized target vol. Output: data/intl/gtaa_weights.json. Render as a 'Country Allocation' table on intl_cycles.html with the HRP weight, regime tilt, and final weight columns. DISPLAY-ONLY until validated with purged K-fold.

upgrades.title: China GTAA: replace static W_REGIME prior with L3 conditional-EV calibrated regime weight
upgrades.spec: In china_masterminds.py: after china_regime_ev.py (L3 upgrade) is validated, replace the static W_TREND=0.30, W_REGIME=0.40 split with a time-varying weight that scales W_REGIME by the current regime_confidence and scales W_TREND by (1 - regime_confidence). When regime_confidence < 0.15 (coin-flip zone, current live state): W_REGIME drops to 0.20, W_TREND rises to 0.50 (trend-following is more reliable in indeterminate regimes). When confidence > 0.60: W_REGIME rises to 0.55, W_TREND drops to 0.20. Implement as a linear interpolation: W_REGIME_eff = clip(0.20 + 0.35 * regime_confidence / 0.60, 0.20, 0.55). Backtest the dynamic vs static weight split on the 2013-2026 GTAA history using walk-forward. Report Sharpe improvement and max drawdown change.

one_line_verdict: All four intl engines (China/HK/Canada/Intl) share the same first-derivative argmax quad template — no base-effect projection, no regime probability distribution, no conditional expected-value engine, no forward vol, no point-in-time validation — making them coincident market-proxy classifiers rather than forward economic forecasts; the HK global-risk overlay and China pathway Wilson-CI are the two genuinely differentiated elements, and both are explicitly display-only.

subsystem: User-facing presentation layer: macro regime / cycle / risk / nowcast UI (macro.html, us_stocks.html, dashboard.html.j2, engine/regime.py, engine/axes.py, engine/playbook.py)

files.role: Primary Jinja2 template rendering macro.html and us_stocks.html — contains the 2x2 quad locator, posture dial, transition radar, Market State board, regime progress bar, and all i18n t()/td() wrappers
Quad classification: raw_quad() argmax, apply_hysteresis() 7-day confirmation state machine, liquidity_overlay() WALCL-based 4-week RoC, cycle_tag() yield-curve/OAS/breadth composite
Growth and inflation axis scoring: score_axis() computes 20d slope z-scored vs 60d trailing window; |z|>0.45 -> +/-1, weighted mean gives axis score in [-1,+1]; confidence = |score|*agreement ratio

Playbook: build_playbook() assembles posture dial (exposure_dial()), historical transition matrix (transition_stats()), next_list probabilities (historical base-rate only), regime progress bar, sector stage table, and 'what's likely next' hover
Conditional forward-distribution kernel: forward_paths(), multi_horizon_cone(), conditional_distribution() — used by anticipation engine on stocks but NOT wired to the macro regime presentation

Scoring thresholds: slope_window=20d, baseline_window=60d, z_threshold=0.45, hysteresis_days=7, shock_override_z=0.85; axis component weights (growth: 6x full-weight market + 4x half-weight econ; inflation: 6x full + 1x half sticky CPI)
Shared navigation partial included by all pages

REGIME LABEL (engine/regime.py + engine/axes.py):
- Each axis: score_axis() computes 10 growth components and 7 inflation components. Each component = score_from_z(slope_z(series, sw=20, bw=60), zt=0.45): the 20-day slope of the series, z-scored against the trailing 60-day distribution of slopes, then mapped -1/0/+1 if |z|>0.45.
- Growth axis (6 full-weight market: copper_gold, xly_xlp, iwm_spy, cyclical_defensive, breadth_direction + 4 half-weight econ: us2y_direction w=0.5, payrolls_trend w=0.5, indpro_trend w=0.5, wei_trend w=0.5, gdpnow_trend w=0.5). Econ confirmers (payrolls, indpro) use monthly_sign(col, periods) = sign of n-month change of a monthly series (axes.py:30-38), not the z-scored slope.
- Inflation axis (6 components at w=1.0: breakeven_10y/5y5y direction, energy_rs, oil_trend, inflation_beta_basket, tips_nominal_momentum w=0.75 + sticky_cpi_direction w=0.5).
- axis_score = weighted mean of available +/-1 scores (NaN = 0, weight excluded). confidence = |axis_score| * agreement_ratio, zeroed if n_comp < 3 (config.yml min_components).
- Quad: raw_quad(g,i) = argmax: g>=0 + i<0 -> Q1; g>=0 + i>=0 -> Q2; g<0 + i>=0 -> Q3; g<0 + i<0 -> Q4. Output: SINGLE argmax label, NOT probabilities.
- Hysteresis (regime.py:41-76): apply_hysteresis() requires new quad to hold 7 consecutive days OR shock_override_z=0.85 single-day magnitude before label flips. pending_quad and pending_days fields track countdown.
- regime_confidence = mean(growth_confidence, inflation_confidence) = scalar in [0,1].

The WEI and GDPNow are ingested as their raw level/direction, not as YoY rates with projected base paths.

one_line_verdict: The presentation layer is well-structured and honest about its limits, but it shows a first-derivative market-proxy argmax with a single point label and historical base-rate hover — missing base-effect forward projection (L1), continuous P(Quad) replacing the {0,1} locator (L2), conditional expected-value per asset (L3), index-level forward distribution cones (L4 — the infrastructure exists in forward_dist.py but is not wired), and a bootstrap CI instead of the heuristic agreement ratio (L6); the two highest-effort/highest-impact gaps for a real-money trader are revised-not-point-in-time data and the absence of any forward uncertainty surface.

current_method:
GTAA ALLOCATION (engine/masterminds.py, lines 173-236): inputs are daily yahoo closes for 9 assets (SPY/QQQ, IEF/TLT, LQD/HYG, GC=F/HG=F, BTC-USD). Four conviction factors:
(1) TREND (W=0.45): tsmom_alloc() — average sign of 63/126/252d returns, skip=5d (cross_asset_trend.py:96-106). Discrete sign, not a continuous signal.
(2) CARRY (W=0.20): z-score of DGS10 (3yr rolling window) for duration; 0.5*y10+0.5*HY-OAS for credit; -real yield (DFII10) for gold. All from latest FRED revision, NOT point-in-time vintages.
(3) REGIME (W=0.20): conditions_frame() percentile-ranked recession_risk + drawdown_risk as risk_off; roro percentile as risk_on. Lagged 2 business days (masterminds.py:73, _LAG=2). Discrete blending: regime[risky] = (-(risk_off-0.5)+(risk_on-0.5)).clip(-1,1). All 4 factors clipped [-1,1] then floored to 0 (long-only).
(4) XMOM (W=0.15): 126d relative rank across the 9 assets, renormalized to [-1,1].
SIZING (masterminds.py:217-236): raw_weight = conviction * (0.10/rv_21d). Per-name cap at prof.w_cap. Vol-target scalar = target_vol/trailing_63d_book_vol, capped at 3.0. Leverage cap via gross normalization. Weekly rebalance every _REBAL=5 bars.
VOL FORECAST (vol_forecast.py:19-38): HAR-style equal-weight blend of close-to-close RV over lags (2,5,22,66d), annualized. No OHLC, no Yang-Zhang, no GARCH/EGARCH.
RISK-BUDGET REFERENCE (portfolio.py): separate, ADDITIVE leaf. 126d covariance window. ERC via damped Maillard-Roncalli fixed point (iters=2000, tol=1e-9, damp=0.5). Output goes to latest.json["portfolio"] — never feeds masterminds weighting.
EQUITY VECTOR ALLOCATION (equity_alloc.py:212-433): 0-100 risk score from 5 legs (drawdown_risk 1.0, recession_risk 1.0, nfci 0.5, hy_widening 0.5, liquidity 0.5) with per-leg publication lags (drawdown=10d, recession=22d, nfci=5d, hy=3d, liq=0d). Glide path with 5-day confirm debounce at 25/50/75 thresholds. Fed-put-gated redeploy overlay on capitulation (cap>=2). No CVaR constraint on drawdown budget.
NET EXPOSURE OVERLAY (net_exposure.py:31-59): two discrete legs — SPX above 200dma (0/1) + net-liq 63d-RoC (0/1). Mean = exposure in {0, 0.5, 1}. Validated on S&P 1927-2026.
MASTER BRAIN LOOP (master_brain.py): LLM synthesis. Reads deterministic outputs (regime, china, hk, commodity, fx, bonds, btc). Stakes falsifiable leans (max 2) logged to data/master_brain/theses.jsonl. master_brain_scorer grades realized outcomes. DOES NOT feed any weight or score.
VALIDATION: deflated_sharpe (Bailey-dePrado) implemented in engine/validation.py. DSR used in research calibrators with n_trials declared. Split-half OOS in active_alloc.split_half_oos. Purged/embargoed walk-forward in research/signal_engine/walk_forward.py (purge=5, embargo=5). Block bootstrap CI available. Meta-labeling implemented as research script. None of purged-CV, triple-barrier, or DSR are wired into the live GTAA allocation scorecard.

gaps: L7 — No HRP (Hierarchical Risk Parity) in the live GTAA allocation. engine/portfolio.py has ERC but it is a display-only reference leaf (additive, never consumed by masterminds.py). The mastermind sizing is inverse-vol with conviction tilt — a risk-parity approximation, not true HRP with hierarchical clustering.

L7 — No Black-Litterman anywhere in the codebase. The regime factor provides a heuristic tilt but there is no formal BL view-blending against a market prior. Regime conviction is hardcoded weights (0.20) with no uncertainty interval.

L7 — No CVaR constraint on the drawdown budget. The vol-target scalar (target_vol/trailing_vol, capped 3x) is the only risk budget enforcement. No conditional-VaR, no explicit DD budget in the optimizer.

L7 — Gross/net dial is static profile knobs (max_lev per profile), not regime-driven. The blueprint calls for min-gross/net-short when P(Q4) is high, max-gross when P(Q1) is high. Current code sets leverage cap as a fixed profile constant regardless of regime state.

L2 — Regime is a hard argmax (raw_quad in regime.py returns a single Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4 label at every bar). No continuous transition probabilities P(Quad_k). No Markov-switching / HMM over the regime axes. The 'confidence' output (regime.py:163) is a mean of growth/inflation confidence scores, not a proper probability.

L1 — Carry factor uses LATEST FRED revision data (DGS10, DFII10, BAMLH0A0HYM2) with only a 2-business-day uniform lag (masterminds.py:73). Monthly macro series (recession_risk, conditions_frame) are acknowledged as needing ALFRED vintages (equity_alloc.py:220,273) but the fix is labeled 'Phase 3' and not yet implemented.

L3 — No per-asset regime-conditional return distribution estimated from historical regime labels. The regime factor (weight 0.20) provides a directional tilt but not a formal E[r_a | quad_k] estimate or CVaR-weighted ranking. There is no 'Hubble' cross-sectional expected-value ranker.

L4 — Vol forecast is close-to-close HAR blend over (2,5,22,66d), no OHLC (no Yang-Zhang, no Parkinson, no Garman-Klass). No GARCH/EGARCH forward vol. The 'heuristic cone' in engine/anticipation.py is a display widget, not a calibrated conditional quantile forecast.

L6 — The live GTAA allocation scorecard does not report DSR (deflated Sharpe) or PBO. DSR is implemented in engine/validation.py and used in calibrator scripts, but is not run against the mastermind backtest to validate the full-sample Sharpe. The split-half OOS is honest but not DSR-adjusted for the number of profile/parameter variants tried.

L6 — Purged K-fold CV and triple-barrier meta-labeling exist only in research scripts (scripts/research/meta_labeling_entry.py, research/signal_engine/walk_forward.py). They are not wired into the live conviction scoring or factor validation pipeline.
L6 — No expectancy / profit-factor / rank-IC broken out by realized regime bucket AND VIX bucket for the GTAA strategies. split_half_oos only reports first/second half CAGR+Sharpe against SPY.

L5 — Vol-control roll-off schedule (high-vol days aging out of trailing window -> mechanical buying) is not tracked. GEX desk (engine/gex_engine.py) exists but its signals do not feed the GTAA allocation. CTA trend flip levels and COT extremes are display-only.

L4 — Forward range is not a calibrated conditional quantile forecast. The anticipation engine (engine/anticipation.py) uses a heuristic cone from HAR vol * scalar, with no measurable coverage target or skewed-t GARCH quantile.

Cross — Master Brain 'research gate' (from memory file mastermind-research-gate) appears to be the LLM synthesis loop, but there is no brain/research_paper.py file found in this worktree — it may be in the Mastermind bot repo (separate, as noted in memory). The dashboard-side brain is context-only and explicitly does NOT gate allocation decisions.
L2 — No time-in-regime hazard function. No forward transition matrix P(Quad_j next | Quad_i now). The transition_state field in the regime output is a label string, not a probability.

upgrades.title: Wire ERC weights from portfolio.py into mastermind sizing as the base risk-parity layer
upgrades.spec: In engine/masterminds.py _weights() (line 217), replace the current raw = conv * (0.10/rv) with: (a) compute 126d trailing covariance of the asset returns, (b) call active_alloc.erc_weights(cov) (already implemented in active_alloc.py:66-92) to get ERC base weights, (c) multiply by conviction tilt (1 + alpha*(conv-0.5)) where alpha is a tuneable tilt strength (default 0.5), (d) apply per-name cap and vol-target scalar as before. Output: ERC weights that satisfy equal risk contribution as the base, tilted by conviction, replacing the heuristic inv-vol approximation. Data: existing yahoo closes already loaded in _prices(). No new collectors needed.

upgrades.title: Regime-driven gross/net dial replacing static profile max_lev constants
upgrades.spec: In engine/masterminds.py _weights() (line 229-233), after per-name capping: read the current regime quad from data/regime/latest.json (or pass it as an argument); map {Q1: 1.0, Q2: 0.85, Q3: 0.70, Q4: 0.50} to a gross_dial scalar; multiply the raw weights by gross_dial before applying the existing leverage cap (prof.max_lev). For the aggressive profile, also apply a net_long_floor = {Q1:0.8, Q2:0.6, Q3:0.4, Q4:0.2}. This makes the leverage dial regime-conditional without requiring HMM probabilities — it is a direct mapping from the existing argmax quad. File: engine/masterminds.py. New config key in config.yml: engine.masterminds.quad_gross_dial: {Q1: 1.0, Q2: 0.85, Q3: 0.70, Q4: 0.50}.
deps: engine/regime.py quad output already in data/regime/latest.json

upgrades.title: DSR + PBO gate on the full mastermind backtest scorecard
upgrades.spec: In scripts/build_masterminds.py _detail_vm() (line 43), after computing bt = M.backtest(pk, P), call engine.validation.deflated_sharpe(bt['scorecard']['sharpe'], skew, kurt, T, n_trials=N_VARIANTS) where N_VARIANTS = number of profile variants ever tried (track in a frozen constant, e.g. 9 = 3 profiles x 3 tuning rounds). Compute skew/kurt from bt['net'] return series. Add dsr, sr0_annual, n_trials to the scorecard dict and expose them in the detail template. Also run block_bootstrap_ci(bt['net']) with B=2000 to get 95% CI on Sharpe/MaxDD. This is the single highest-honesty-per-effort upgrade: validation.deflated_sharpe already exists and is tested.

upgrades.title: ALFRED point-in-time lag fix for FRED macro carry inputs
upgrades.spec: In engine/masterminds.py _conviction() carry block (lines 184-191): add per-series release lags matching equity_alloc.LEG_LAGS: DGS10 -> lag 2d (market rate, daily), BAMLH0A0HYM2 -> lag 2d, DFII10 -> lag 2d. These are already market-traded series so the lag is minimal — but apply .shift(lag) before z-scoring to be explicit. For the regime factor inputs (recession_risk/drawdown_risk/roro from conditions_frame): the 2-business-day uniform lag (_LAG=2 at line 73) under-lags monthly recession series. Update _LAG to 22 for the recession_risk leg specifically, matching equity_alloc.LEG_LAGS['recession']. Use the same _assemble_legs() pattern already in equity_alloc.py:236-261. Long-run fix: consume ALFRED real-time vintages via the Philly Fed API for the monthly series.

upgrades.title: Regime-conditional return distribution (mu_{a,k}) estimated per quad
upgrades.spec: Add engine/regime_conditional_ev.py. For each asset a in the mastermind universe and each quad k in {Q1,Q2,Q3,Q4}: (1) load the full returns_frame() and the historical regime labels from data/regime/regime_history (regime.py already writes this), (2) compute mu_{a,k} = mean weekly return of asset a on weeks where the confirmed quad = k, and sigma_{a,k} = std, using POINT-IN-TIME regime labels (shift regime by 1 week before merging with returns), (3) output a dict {quad: {asset: {mu, sigma, n}}} to data/regime/conditional_ev.json, (4) in masterminds.py _conviction(), add a fifth factor (W_CEV=0.10, reducing W_TREND to 0.35) that is the z-score of mu_{a,k} across assets within the current quad. This is the L3 expected-value ranker slotted as a fifth conviction factor. Note: n_obs per quad will be small (10-40 weekly observations) — must display honest N and wide CIs alongside.

upgrades.title: Yang-Zhang OHLC realized vol in vol_forecast.py (replace close-to-close)
upgrades.spec: In engine/vol_forecast.py, add yang_zhang_vol(open, high, low, close, win) function implementing the Yang-Zhang (2000) OHLC estimator: sigma_YZ^2 = sigma_O^2 + k*sigma_C^2 + (1-k)*sigma_RS^2 where sigma_O = Rogers-Satchell open-to-close component, sigma_C = close-to-open (overnight), sigma_RS = Rogers-Satchell. k = 0.34/(1.34 + (n+1)/(n-1)). In engine/masterminds.py _weights(): check if OHLC columns (open/high/low) exist in store.read('yahoo', asset); if yes, use yang_zhang_vol; else fall back to har_vol on close. Yahoo parquet files have OHLC columns already (they are stored as close only per memory note 'yahoo close is total return' — verify if high/low/open are stored; if not, this upgrade requires adding OHLC to the yahoo collector). Effort escalates to L if OHLC collection needs adding.
deps: verify yahoo parquet OHLC column availability in data/yahoo/

upgrades.title: Regime transition matrix P(Quad_j | Quad_i) from historical quad series
upgrades.spec: Add engine/regime_transition.py. Load data/regime/regime_history (quad column). Compute the empirical weekly transition matrix T[i,j] = count(quad_{t+1}=j | quad_t=i) / count(quad_t=i) for i,j in {Q1,Q2,Q3,Q4}. Apply Laplace smoothing (add 1 to each count). Compute stationary distribution and time-in-regime hazard (mean+std of consecutive same-quad runs). Output to data/regime/transition_matrix.json. In masterminds.py _weights(): when the current quad is confirmed, read P(next_quad) from the transition matrix; if P(Q4 next) > 0.4, cap gross_dial at 0.7 as a forward-looking de-risk overlay. In the display: render the 4x4 transition heatmap on the regime page. No HMM required — this is the empirical frequency matrix, fully interpretable. Note: historical regime labels are point-in-time only from the date regime.py was deployed; pre-deployment labels use today's weights applied to historical data (survivorship/revision risk).
deps: data/regime/regime_history — quad column present per engine/regime.py:75

upgrades.title: CVaR drawdown budget constraint in mastermind sizing
upgrades.spec: In engine/masterminds.py _weights() (line 217), after computing raw weights and before the vol-target scale: (1) simulate a 1-step parametric CVaR from the trailing 126d return distribution: for each asset compute the 5th percentile of the 21d return window, (2) compute book CVaR = sum(w_i * CVaR_i) + correlation_adjustment where correlation_adjustment = sum_ij(w_i*w_j*cov_ij * z_5pct_factor), (3) if book_CVaR exceeds a profile-specific CVaR budget (conservative=-0.07, moderate=-0.12, aggressive=-0.22 annualized), scale weights down uniformly until the budget is met before applying the vol-target scalar. This gives a second risk check beyond vol-targeting that is sensitive to left-tail asymmetry. The CVaR budget can be set to match the same numeric threshold as target_vol for a first pass.

upgrades.title: Scorecard broken out by realized regime bucket and VIX bucket
upgrades.spec: In engine/active_alloc.py, add regime_split_scorecard(net: pd.Series, regime_history: pd.DataFrame, vix: pd.Series) function. Split net returns into: (a) 4 regime buckets by the confirmed quad in regime_history, (b) 3 VIX buckets (VIX<15, 15-25, >25). For each bucket compute CAGR, Sharpe, max-DD, n_obs. Expose in scripts/build_masterminds.py as a collapsible 'regime breakdown' table on the detail page. Data: data/regime/regime_history (quad), data/yahoo/_VIX.parquet. This replaces the current single split_half_oos with a richer decomposition that reveals whether the edge is regime-conditional.

upgrades.title: Wire L5 GEX gamma-flip level as a vol-context input to the vol-target scalar
upgrades.spec: engine/gex_engine.py already computes a gamma_flip level. In engine/masterminds.py _weights(), after computing port_vol: read the latest gamma_flip level from the gex snapshot (data/gex/ or latest.json['gex']); if SPX is within 1% of the gamma_flip level (either side), multiply the vol-target scalar by 0.80 to pre-emptively de-gross into the potential gamma-cliff vol spike. This is a low-effort mechanical-flow overlay that is orthogonal to all other factors. No new data collection needed.

one_line_verdict: The portfolio construction layer has a working, honestly-scored conviction-weighted vol-targeted GTAA engine with a clean cost model and split-half OOS, but it is missing the three specific L7 blueprint ingredients — HRP base (ERC exists but is display-only), Black-Litterman view-blending (no BL anywhere), and a regime-conditional CVaR drawdown budget — while the regime dial is static per-profile knobs rather than P(Quad)-driven gross/net; close-to-close vol only; no DSR on the live mastermind scorecard; and all macro carry inputs use latest-revision FRED data without ALFRED point-in-time vintages.
